title: Mepal — 75 (NZ) Squadron Memorial Garden
memorial_type: Memorial Garden — rose garden with octagonal base and circular memorial stone
memorial_address: Corner of Laurel Close and High Street, Mepal, East Cambridgeshire CB6 2BN
erected_by: Former members of 75 New Zealand Squadron RAF
inscription: This Plinth was donated by former members of 75 NEW ZEALAND SQUADRON R.A.F. stationed at Mepal between 1943 and 1945 IN REMEMBRANCE OF THOSE WHO FAILED TO RETURN
narrative: 75 (New Zealand) Squadron was the RNZAF's primary heavy bomber unit within Bomber Command, flying Stirlings and then Lancasters from RAF Mepal in Cambridgeshire from 1943 to 1945. The squadron drew heavily from New Zealand manpower and also flew with Australian, British, and Canadian crew. The human cost was severe: over 200 aircrew were killed from RAF Mepal operations. The memorial garden at the corner of Laurel Close and High Street in Mepal village was donated by former members of the squadron and dedicated on 26 August 1978 by the Rector of Mepal, with 350 veterans in attendance — a remarkable gathering thirty-three years after the war. The rose garden centres on an octagonal base with a circular memorial stone. The garden is maintained and accessible year-round in the village centre.
memorial_details: Rose garden with lawn area in village centre at corner of Laurel Close and High Street, Mepal. Octagonal base with circular memorial stone donated by former members of 75 NZ Squadron. Dedicated 26 August 1978 by Revd John Bidder, Rector of Mepal, with 350 veterans present. Accessible and maintained. IWM War Memorials Register reference: IWM 46526.
